Wanting something starts with knowing what you're done with.

Kevin explains that before the vision and the goal comes a simpler step. Ask what in your life you will no longer tolerate and are fed up with.

He runs through everyday examples: the car, the home, the clothes, the bank balance, the maxed-out credit cards. His point is that you need some pain to get you to move.

What are you most ready to stop tolerating?

The one habit Kevin says keeps people stuck in place.

Kevin recalls a book called The Magic of Thinking Big, whose first chapter says believe you can succeed and you will. He loves the title of the second chapter, which is about dropping the excuse habit.

A man once told him that failures are always good at one thing: making excuses. Kevin's answer is to believe in yourself and in your dream.

Which excuse shows up most often for you?

A better goal than more money, in Kevin's words.

Kevin Trudeau says you have more power within you than you realize. But more than anything else, he wants you to wake up and say, "I love my life."

Then, through the day, say, "I love being me." He asks whether that wouldn't be the ultimate.

Could you say those two sentences and mean them today?

#ad #happiness #mindset #success

Two people take the same class. Only one becomes great.

Kevin Trudeau gives an example. Two friends learn piano together, five days a week for a year. One plays fantastic and the other plays just okay. He says it comes down to natural ability.

The same goes for sports, where one kid always seems a natural. Kevin says we can all improve our abilities, but some people simply start with more.

Where do you think your natural ability lies?
